translations.text: When it was late on that day, the first day of the week: and so on.
"After the Saviour's resurrection his disciples were shut in a house for fear of the Jewish people:" and so on.
Now the evangelist John says that the Saviour performed many other signs in the sight of his disciples which were not set down in Christ's books.
These miracles are written so that you may believe that the Saviour is the Son of God, and that you may have eternal life through that faith.
Now Pope Gregory expounds this gospel, and says that everyone wonders how the Saviour came in to his apostles, even though the doors were shut.
Again the holy Gregory says that Christ's body came in through closed doors, the same body that was born of the maiden Mary from a closed womb.
What wonder is it that the Saviour came in with an eternal body through locked doors, when with a mortal body he was born from the closed womb of the maiden?
We read in the book called the Acts of the Apostles that the chief men of the Jewish people put Christ's apostles in prison:

Then in the night an angel of God came to them and led them out of the prison, and in the morning the prison stood securely locked. God can do all things: now we must marvel at his might, and also believe.
He showed the body to be touched, the same body that he had brought in through closed doors. His body could be touched, and yet it was incorruptible;
he showed himself as able to be touched and as incorruptible, because his body was of the same nature that it had been before, but it was nevertheless of a different glory.
The Saviour said to them, "Peace be among you." Christ came to men for the sake of peace, and he proclaimed and taught peace, and nothing is pleasing to him that is done without peace.
"As my Father sent me, so I send you. The Father loves the Son, and yet he sent him to suffering for the redemption of mankind."

Christ also loved his apostles, and yet he did not make them kings, or nobles, or give them worldly joy; instead he sent them throughout the whole world to preach baptism and the faith that he himself taught.
They preached until the wicked killed them, and they went victorious to their Lord.
Christ breathed on the apostles and said, "Receive the Holy Spirit." The Holy Spirit came upon the apostles twice: once now, and again a second time after Christ's ascension.
While he was still living on earth, Christ breathed the Holy Spirit upon the apostles as a sign that every Christian must love his neighbour as himself.
Afterwards, when he had ascended to heaven, he sent the same Spirit upon the apostles in the form of fire, as a sign that we must love God above all other things.
The Holy Spirit is one, though he came upon the apostles twice. So too there is one love but two commandments: that we must love God and men.
But we must learn through people how we can come to the love of God, just as John the apostle said,
"He who does not love his brother, whom he sees, how can he love God, whom he does not see bodily?"
Before that time the Holy Spirit was dwelling in the apostles, but they were not so strongly inspired that they could preach God's faith so boldly,
as they afterwards could, through the grace of the Holy Spirit. They sat shut up in a house for fear of the Jewish people;
but after they were filled with the Holy Spirit, they became so emboldened and so brave that they freely preached the name of God to fierce and cruel kings.
Christ said to the apostles, "The sins of those people whom you forgive are forgiven them; and from those from whom you withhold forgiveness, it is withheld."
Christ gave this power to the apostles and to all bishops, if they hold it rightly.
But if the bishop acts according to his own will, and wants to bind the innocent and loose the guilty, then he loses the power that God gave him.
He must grant forgiveness of sins to those people whom he sees to be moved to contrition through God's grace, and he must be hard toward those who have no repentance for their misdeeds.
Christ raised the stinking Lazarus from death, and when he was alive, he said to his disciples,
"Loose his bonds, so that he may walk." Then they loosed the bonds of the revived man whom Christ had raised to life.
Therefore teachers must unbind from their sins those whom Christ brings to life through compunction.
Every sinful man who hides his sins lies dead in the tomb; but if he confesses his sins through compunction, then he comes out of the tomb, as Lazarus did when Christ commanded him to arise:
then the teacher must release him from eternal punishment, just as the apostles bodily loosed Lazarus.
But the layman must fear the bishop's sentence, even if he is innocent, lest he become guilty through pride.
It did not happen to the apostle Thomas without providence that he did not believe in Christ's resurrection; rather, it happened through God's providence, for through his touching we are believers.
His doubting did us more good than the faith of the other apostles, because when he was brought to faith by touching, the doubt was thereby taken away from us.
Christ could easily have risen from death without the scars of his wounds, but he kept the scars because he wished to strengthen the doubters with them. He said to Thomas,
"You believe because you have seen me." He saw the body and the scars, and he believed that he was God, who raised the body from death.
These words that follow here gladden us greatly: "Blessed are those who have not seen me, and yet believe in me."
By that saying all those are signified who have not seen Christ in the body, and yet hold him in their hearts through faith.
He truly believes in God who carries out in his works what he believes. He who professes that he knows God, and does evil works, denies God by those works.
Faith that is without good works is dead. These are the words of the apostles; receive them with a careful mind.

We are speaking about the resurrection. Now there are some people who have doubts about the resurrection, and when they see the bones of dead people, they say, "How can these bones be brought back to life?"
As if they were speaking wisely! But we say in reply that God is Almighty and can do all that he wills. He made the heavens and the earth and all creatures without any material.

Now it seems that it would be in some ways easier for him to raise the dead from the dust than it was for him to make all creatures from nothing; but in truth all things are equally easy for him, and nothing is difficult.
He made Adam from clay. Now we cannot comprehend how he made from that clay flesh and blood, bone and skin, hair and nails.
People often see that from one little seed comes a great tree, but we cannot see in the seed either root, or bark, or boughs, or leaves;
but the God who brings forth from the kernel a tree, and fruits, and leaves, that same God can raise up from dust flesh and bone, sinews and hair, just as he said in his gospel,
"Not one hair of your head shall be lost to you."
The apostle Paul said that we shall rise from death at the age that Christ was when he suffered, that is, about thirty-three years.
Though a child dies, or a man worn out with age, they nevertheless come to the age that we spoke of before;
Yet each one will have his own stature, which he had in this life, or would have had if he had lived long enough to reach it.
If anyone was crippled or lacked limbs in this life, he will then be as it is written: "All those who belong to God's kingdom have neither blemish nor deformity in their body."
Why should we inquire about the others who depart to eternal perdition, whether they are maimed or limbless, when they are dwelling in eternal torment?

It will then be just as Christ said: "No man will take a wife, nor will a woman take a husband, nor will offspring be begotten, nor will they taste death afterwards, but they will be like the angels, since they will dwell with the angels."
Nor will they desire any lust, nor will they ever afterwards commit sins. There will be no sorrow there, nor pain, nor any affliction, but there will be perfect peace and everlasting bliss,
and both those who were known before and those who were unknown will be known to one another, dwelling in brotherly love with God forever into eternity. Amen.
